answer: Bind each agent identity to a scarce external namespace: to register, it must prove control of a distinct DNS domain by publishing a beacon-seeded TXT record every epoch. Like dredging one ferrous nugget from an ocean of cheap aliases, the chain admits only a single identity per verified, continuously-renewed domain — a short sonnet of proof re-sung each round. A sybil fleet then needs N genuinely registered, separately-paid domains, each kept live, so forgery costs linear registrar fees plus perpetual upkeep instead of one free mint.
